title: The Town Where You're Not Allowed to Die
sources: Visit Svalbard FAQ: not illegal to die; coffin burials not permitted; permafrost affects decomposition and freeze-thaw slowly pushes coffins upward
Polar Journal 2020: Longyearbyen cemetery used for coffin burials 1918-1950, including seven Spanish flu victims; afterwards the deceased taken to the mainland
Mental Floss / IFLScience 2018: no law against dying; small hospital, seriously ill sent to mainland Norway
Norway Today 2020 / Shared Histories Canada: 1997-98 exhumation of 1918 flu victims in Longyearbyen; virus traces found

lines.text: There's a town in the Arctic where people say dying is against the law.
Olaf lives in Longyearbyen, and one morning he wakes up feeling awful.
So he walks into the tiny hospital,
and the doctor just hands him a plane ticket.
I'm sick, not going on holiday!
So Olaf storms up to the cemetery to prove her wrong,
but the newest grave is from nineteen fifty,
lines.caps: but | the newest | grave | is from | 1950,

lines.text: and the old coffins are creeping up out of the ground.
Well, the town sits on permafrost, so bodies here don't rot. They freeze.
Scientists even found traces of the nineteen eighteen flu still inside them.
lines.caps: Scientists | even found | traces | of the | 1918 | flu | still | inside them.

lines.text: And every summer the ground thaws and refreezes, pushing coffins back up.
So dying was never illegal. There's just no ground that will keep you.
Olaf grabs the ticket. Fine. But I'm coming back alive.
